mainTopic: חנניה's view that the father counts in אותו ואת בנו, and whether רבי יהודה is sure or in doubt that the father doesn't count in deciding a mule's species
overview: The גמרא first gives חנניה's source from the פסוק: 'אותו' points to a male parent and 'בנו' points to a female, so אותו ואת בנו covers both. שמואל rules like חנניה. The גמרא shows this fits שמואל's comment on a משנה in כלאים. There, רבי יהודה looks only at the mother to decide an animal's species, while the חכמים, who are חנניה, also count the father. The גמרא then asks whether רבי יהודה is sure the father doesn't count or is only in doubt. The practical difference is whether a mule may mate with its mother's species. A proof from the משנה and a proof from a ברייתא about a female mule are both pushed away. Then רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע says everyone forbids mating the offspring with its mother's species, so רבי יהודה is in doubt. Finally, a story shows that רבי אבא matched his wagon mules only by signs of the mother, so he holds that the father does not count.

steps.title: חנניה's source for including both males and females
steps.stepSummary: חנניה learns from 'אותו' (male) and 'בנו' (female) that the איסור applies to both.
steps.simpleTranslation: According to חנניה: the פסוק says 'אותו' (it), which implies a male. It also says 'בנו' (its offspring), meaning the parent its offspring clings to, which implies a female. So the law applies to both males and females.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the reason behind חנניה's opinion that אותו ואת בנו applies to fathers as well as mothers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'אותו' is grammatically masculine, so it hints at a male parent. The phrase 'בנו' describes the parent a young animal follows around, and that is the mother. Since the פסוק hints at both, חנניה includes both.

keyTerms.meaning: 'It' (masculine form), here read as pointing to a male parent
Clings after it, follows it around

phrases.english: And according to Ḥananya,
it is written "it," which implies a male,
and it is written "its offspring" —
meaning the one whose offspring clings after it,
phrases.notes: A baby animal follows its mother around, so this phrase points to the mother.

phrases.english: which implies a female;
therefore it applies both to males
and to females.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the earlier explanation of each side's source, now giving חנניה's.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to חנניה, אותו ואת בנו applies to both male and female parents, based on 'אותו' and 'בנו'.

steps.title: שמואל rules like חנניה
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא בר חייא quotes שמואל: the הלכה follows חנניה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא בר חייא said in the name of שמואל: the הלכה is like חנניה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a practical ruling: we follow חנניה, so the איסור applies to a father animal and its offspring too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This settles the מחלוקת in favor of חנניה, even though the anonymous view disagreed with him. The next steps will show this ruling fits a position שמואל holds elsewhere.
steps.whyThisMatters: According to שמואל's ruling, the איסור of אותו ואת בנו also covers a male animal and its known offspring.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא בַּר חִיָּיא אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל:
phrases.english: Rav Huna bar Ḥiyya says that Shmuel says:
The halakha is in accordance with Ḥananya,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After hearing חנניה's reason, we get the practical ruling in his favor.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The הלכה follows חנניה: אותו ואת בנו applies to males as well.

steps.title: שמואל is consistent: the משנה about horse and donkey offspring
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says שמואל follows his own reasoning and quotes רבי יהודה's view in a משנה about mixed offspring.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל follows his own reasoning, as we learned in a משנה: רבי יהודה says, animals born from a mother horse may mate with each other, even if the father of one is a donkey. But animals born from a mother donkey may not mate with animals born from a mother horse.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sets up a proof that שמואל's ruling fits his view elsewhere. First it quotes the משנה that he commented on.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי יהודה, only the mother decides an animal's species. So any two animals born from mother horses count as one species, whoever the fathers were. Two mules with different mothers, one a horse and one a donkey, count as different species and are forbidden to mate as כלאים.

keyTerms.meaning: He follows his own line of reasoning (is consistent)
Permitted to mate with one another
Forbidden mixing of species (the topic of this משנה)

phrases.english: And Shmuel follows his line of reasoning,
as we learned in a mishna: Rabbi Yehuda says:
Those born from a horse,
even if their father is a donkey,
are permitted with one another;
but those born from a donkey
together with those born from a horse
are forbidden.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins showing that שמואל's ruling for חנניה matches his approach elsewhere.
steps.raayaObject: That שמואל's ruling like חנניה is consistent with his other statements.
steps.raayaSupportSource: משנה כלאים 8:4 (רבי יהודה on horse and donkey offspring), together with שמואל's comment on it.

steps.title: שמואל: רבי יהודה ignores the father, the חכמים do not
steps.stepSummary: שמואל explains that רבי יהודה ignores the father, while the חכמים say all mules are one species.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: this is the view of רבי יהודה, who says we do not pay attention to the father's seed. But the חכמים say all kinds of mules are one species.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings שמואל's own comment on that משנה, which sets up two sides: רבי יהודה and the חכמים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה looks only at the mother. The חכמים look at both parents. So a mule with a horse mother and donkey father, and a mule with a donkey mother and horse father, are both 'half horse, half donkey' and count as one species.

keyTerms.meaning: We do not take the father's seed into account

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two names: רבי יהודה is the תנא in the משנה, while רב יהודה is the אמורא quoting שמואל.

phrases.english: And Rav Yehuda says that Shmuel says:
This is the statement of Rabbi Yehuda,
who says we are not concerned with the father's seed;
but the Rabbis say:
All types of mules are one.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל: זוֹ דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds שמואל's comment on the משנה just quoted.
steps.raayaObject: שמואל's view on whether the father matters in deciding species.
steps.raayaSupportSource: שמואל's statement that רבי יהודה ignores the father while the חכמים treat all mules as one species.

steps.title: Identifying the חכמים as חנניה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks who the חכמים are and answers that they are חנניה, who counts the father, so all mules are one species.
steps.simpleTranslation: Who are these חכמים? It is חנניה, who says we do take the father into account. So this one, from a horse and a donkey, and that one, from a donkey and a horse, are all one species.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא connects the two topics: the חכמים in כלאים are חנניה, the same תנא שמואל followed in אותו ואת בנו.
steps.deeperAnalysis: חנניה counts the father in אותו ואת בנו, and the same idea, that the father counts, explains why all mules are one species. So שמואל is consistent: in both places he follows the view that the father matters.

keyTerms.meaning: We take the father's seed into account

steps.whatToRemember: חנניה: the father counts, both for אותו ואת בנו and for deciding species. שמואל follows חנניה, so his two rulings fit together.

phrases.english: Who are the Rabbis?
It is Ḥananya,
who says we are concerned with the father's seed;
and this one, offspring of a horse and a donkey,
phrases.notes: Here the mother is the horse and the father is the donkey.

phrases.english: and that one, offspring of a donkey and a horse,
they are all one species.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains who the חכמים in שמואל's statement are, which ties the כלאים discussion back to חנניה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which תנא is meant by the 'חכמים' who say all mules are one species?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: It is חנניה, who counts the father, so mules from either combination count as one species.

steps.title: Is רבי יהודה sure or unsure about ignoring the father?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether רבי יהודה is certain that the father does not count, or whether he is only in doubt.
steps.simpleTranslation: A question was asked: Is רבי יהודה sure that we ignore the father's side, or is he just unsure about it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new question about רבי יהודה's view from the previous steps. It wants to know how firm his position is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 4 we learned that רבי יהודה does not take the father into account. Now the גמרא asks whether that is a firm ruling (the father truly does not matter) or only a doubt (maybe the father matters, maybe not).

keyTerms.meaning: A question was asked (a real open question the חכמים were unsure about)
It is clear to him; he is sure
We do not worry about the father's seed (the father does not set the species)
He is in doubt about it

phrases.english: A question was asked of them:
Is it clear to Rabbi Yehuda
that we are not concerned with the father's seed,
or perhaps he is in doubt about it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on רבי יהודה's view from steps 3-4 and asks how certain it is.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether רבי יהודה's rule of ignoring the father is certain or only a doubt.

steps.title: The practical difference: mating with the mother's species
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what difference the question makes and answers that it decides whether a mule may mate with its mother's species.
steps.simpleTranslation: What difference does it make? It matters for allowing the offspring to mate with the mother's species. If he is sure, that is allowed. If he is unsure, it is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא first checks that the question has a real practical result, and then gives one: mating the offspring with an animal of its mother's species.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Take a mule born from a female horse and a male donkey. If רבי יהודה is sure the father does not count, this mule is simply a horse, so it may mate with a horse. If he is only unsure, maybe it is part donkey, so mating it with a horse could be כלאים and must be forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: What practical difference does it make?

phrases.english: What difference does it make?
For permitting the offspring with the mother,
phrases.notes: "The mother" here means the mother's species. If the mother was a horse, think of mating the mule with a horse.

phrases.english: if you say: it is clear to him,
the offspring with the mother is permitted,

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא אִי אָמְרַתְּ: סַפּוֹקֵי מְסַפְּקָא לֵיהּ –
phrases.english: but if you say: he is in doubt about it,
the offspring with the mother is forbidden.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows that the question in step 6 has a real result.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What practical result depends on whether רבי יהודה is sure or unsure.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Mating a mule with its mother's species is permitted if he is sure and forbidden if he is unsure.

steps.title: Bringing רבי יהודה's words from the משנה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings רבי יהודה's statement that all animals born from a female horse may mate with each other, even if a father was a donkey.
steps.simpleTranslation: So what is the answer? Come and hear: רבי יהודה says: All animals born from a horse, even if their father is a donkey, may mate with one another.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings רבי יהודה's words from the משנה to try to answer the question. This step only quotes the source, and the next step will work out what it proves.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under רבי יהודה, animals that share a horse mother may mate together even when a father was a donkey. The גמרא has not yet explained how this answers the question. It first has to pin down exactly which case the משנה is talking about.

keyTerms.meaning: Permitted with one another (allowed to mate together)

phrases.english: What? Come and hear:
Rabbi Yehuda says:
All that are born from a horse,
even though their father is a donkey,
are permitted with one another.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a source to settle the question from step 6.
steps.raayaObject: Whether רבי יהודה is sure that the father does not count.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי יהודה's statement in the משנה about animals born from a horse.

steps.title: Which case is the משנה talking about?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא shows that the משנה cannot mean two mules that both have donkey fathers, because that would be obvious. So it must mean one with a horse father and one with a donkey father.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the case? If both animals have donkey fathers, why would we need to be told? So it must be that one animal's father is a horse and the other's father is a donkey.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא works out which case the משנה is describing by ruling out the obvious one. This sets up the proof in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If both animals came from a horse mother and a donkey father, they are exactly the same mix, so of course they may mate. A משנה would not need to say that. So the משנה must mean a pure horse (horse father) together with a mule (donkey father), where the fathers are different.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the case? What are the exact circumstances?
If we say (a first suggestion that will be rejected)
Does it need to be said? (It is obvious)
Rather, is it not that... (the suggestion that is left)

phrases.english: What is the case?
If we say that this one's father is a donkey
phrases.notes: "This one" and "that one" are the two animals being mated. Both have a horse mother.

phrases.english: and that one's father is a donkey,
does it need to be said?
Rather, is it not that this one's father is a horse
and that one's father is a donkey?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Works out which case the source in step 8 means, so it can be used as a proof.
steps.raayaObject: Whether רבי יהודה is sure that the father does not count.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The case in the משנה must be animals with different fathers, since the case of identical fathers is obvious.

steps.title: Conclusion: רבי יהודה is sure
steps.stepSummary: Since the משנה allows animals with a horse father and a donkey father to mate, רבי יהודה must be sure that the father does not count.
steps.simpleTranslation: And yet it teaches that they may mate with each other. So it is clear to him that the father does not count.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes this attempted proof that רבי יהודה is certain. The next step rejects it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If רבי יהודה were only unsure about the father, he would have to forbid mating a horse-father animal with a donkey-father animal, since maybe they are different species. Because he permits it, he must hold for sure that only the mother counts.
steps.whatToRemember: According to this proof, רבי יהודה is sure that the father does not count at all. So a mule from a horse mother is treated as a horse and may mate with a horse.
steps.whyThisMatters: If this proof held, it would settle the practical difference from step 7 in favor of permitting. But step 11 rejects it, and step 21 concludes the opposite.

phrases.english: and yet it teaches that they are permitted with each other,
evidently it is clear to him!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְקָתָנֵי מוּתָּרִים זֶה עִם זֶה, אַלְמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the proof from the case worked out in step 9.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: This attempted proof would show רבי יהודה is certain, but step 11 rejects it.

steps.title: Maybe both mules have donkey fathers
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof from steps 9-10. The משנה may really be talking about two mules whose fathers are both donkeys.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. Really, the father of this mule is a donkey, and the father of that mule is also a donkey.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא says 'No' to the proof it just built. It goes back to the reading it had thrown out: both mules have donkey fathers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 9 had said this reading was too obvious to need saying, so the משנה must mean a horse father and a donkey father. Now the גמרא brings back the 'both donkey fathers' reading. If it holds, the משנה no longer proves that רבי יהודה is sure the father does not count. The next step will explain why the משנה would still need to say it.

keyTerms.meaning: Really / actually. Used when going back to a reading that was set aside.

phrases.english: No,
actually, the father of this one is a donkey,
phrases.notes: 'This one' is the male mule. 'That one' in the next line is the female mule.

phrases.english: and the father of that one is a donkey.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the conclusion of step 10 by bringing back the reading that step 9 had thrown out.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof from the משנה that רבי יהודה is sure the father does not count.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The משנה could be about two mules that both have donkey fathers. Then it says nothing about a horse father together with a donkey father.

steps.title: Why the משנה still needed to say it
steps.stepSummary: Even when both mules have donkey fathers, the משנה had to teach that they may mate. Otherwise we might think each one's horse side mates with the other's donkey side.
steps.simpleTranslation: And you asked: does this need to be said? Yes. You might have thought that the horse side of one mule mates with the donkey side of the other, and the donkey side mates with the horse side. That would be mixing species. So the משנה teaches us that they may mate.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the 'it's obvious' argument from step 9. It explains what new idea the משנה teaches even if both fathers are donkeys.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A mule is part horse and part donkey. One might picture the horse part of the male joining with the donkey part of the female, and the other way around, which would be כלאים. The משנה teaches that two such mules count as one kind, so the ruling is not obvious after all.

keyTerms.meaning: Does it need to be said? An argument that a ruling is too obvious.
You might have thought... so it teaches us. This shows what new idea a ruling adds.
Side / part. Here, the horse part or the donkey part of a mule.
Mates with (a polite way of saying it)

phrases.english: And as for what you said: does it need to be said?
phrases.notes: This points back to step 9, where the גמרא said the 'both donkey fathers' reading was too obvious.

phrases.english: You might have said:

phrases.aramaic: אָתֵי צַד דְּסוּס מִשְׁתַּמֵּשׁ בְּצַד חֲמוֹר,
phrases.english: the horse side comes and mates with the donkey side,
and the donkey side mates with the horse side,
so it teaches us that they may mate.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the rejection in step 11 by answering step 9's claim that this reading is obvious.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows that the ruling teaches something new
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Two mules mating might count as כלאים, since each one's horse side would join the other's donkey side.
steps.terutzMaskana: Two mules with donkey fathers count as the same kind and may mate.
steps.whatToRemember: The proof from the משנה is gone. The משנה can be about two mules with donkey fathers, so it does not show whether רבי יהודה is sure or in doubt. Steps 20-21 give the final answer.

steps.title: A ברייתא suggests רבי יהודה is in doubt
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה says a female mule may not be mated with a horse or a donkey, only with her own kind. If he were sure the father does not count, he should allow her mother's species.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come hear: רבי יהודה says, a female mule in heat may not be mated with a horse or a donkey, only with her own kind. If you say he is sure, why not mate her with her mother's species?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new source, a ברייתא, to answer the question from step 6. This one points the other way: רבי יהודה is in doubt.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If only the mother counts, a mule born from a female horse is simply a horse, so a horse should be allowed to mate with her. רבי יהודה forbids both a horse and a donkey. That suggests he worries that the father might also count.

keyTerms.meaning: That is in heat (literally, that 'asked' for a mate)

phrases.english: Come hear: Rabbi Yehuda says,
a female mule that is in heat,
we do not mate with her
neither a horse nor a donkey,
only her own kind.
And if you say he is sure that the father does not count,
then let us mate her with her mother's species!

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר, פִּרְדָּה שֶׁתָּבְעָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the proof from the משנה fell, the גמרא tries a new source that points the other way.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי יהודה is in doubt about whether the father counts.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא: רבי יהודה forbids mating a female mule with a horse or a donkey.

steps.title: Maybe we don't know her mother's species
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא may be talking about a mule whose mother's species is unknown.
steps.simpleTranslation: The ברייתא is about a case where we don't know what her mother's species is.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the proof. Maybe רבי יהודה forbids a horse and a donkey only because we don't know which one was her mother.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the mother's species is unknown, then even someone who is sure only the mother counts cannot pick a mate. Either choice might be the wrong species. So the ruling does not prove that רבי יהודה is in doubt about the father.

phrases.english: It is a case where we do not know
what her mother's species is.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּלָא יָדְעִינַן מִינָא דְּאִמַּהּ מַאי נִיהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof in step 13 by limiting the ברייתא to a special case.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof from the ברייתא that רבי יהודה is in doubt.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The ruling can be explained by not knowing the mother's species, not by doubt about the father.

steps.title: But the ברייתא says 'her own kind'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges step 14. The words 'only her own kind' sound like we know exactly what she is.
steps.simpleTranslation: But the ברייתא teaches 'only her own kind'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer in step 14 using the ברייתא's own words.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Saying 'her own kind' sounds like her species is known. That seems to clash with the idea that we don't know what her mother was.

keyTerms.meaning: But it teaches! Used to challenge from the wording of a source.

phrases.english: But it teaches 'only her own kind'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer in step 14.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim in step 14 that the mother's species is unknown.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The words 'her own kind' suggest that her kind is known.

steps.title: Reading the ברייתא as giving a reason
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rereads the ברייתא. A horse or donkey is not allowed because we usually don't know her species.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what it means: we don't mate a horse or a donkey with her, because we don't know her species.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by explaining what the ברייתא really means.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this reading, the ברייתא is giving the reason horses and donkeys are not allowed: her mother's species usually isn't known. So the ban on a horse or a donkey comes from not knowing her mother, not from doubt about the father.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what it means (rereading a source)

phrases.english: This is what it is saying:
we do not mate with her

phrases.aramaic: לֹא מִין סוּס וְלֹא מִין חֲמוֹר,
phrases.english: neither the horse species nor the donkey species,
because we do not know her species.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 15.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Her own kind' means her species is known.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא forbids a horse or donkey because her mother's species is unknown, not because of doubt about the father.

steps.title: Why not check her by signs?
steps.stepSummary: Signs like voice, ears and tail can show what the mother was. So why not use them?
steps.simpleTranslation: Let us check by signs! As אביי said: a deep voice means the mother was a donkey, a shrill voice means the mother was a horse. And רב פפא said: big ears and a small tail mean the mother was a donkey, small ears and a big tail mean the mother was a horse.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges again. The mother's species can be found out, so 'we don't know' should not be a problem.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If physical signs show the mother's species, we can find out what she is and mate her with that species. Then the ban on horses and donkeys again looks like doubt about the father.

phrases.english: But let him check by signs?
As Abaye said:
if its voice is deep, it is the child of a donkey,
phrases.notes: 'Child of a donkey' means its mother was a donkey. These signs tell us about the mother.

phrases.english: if its voice is shrill, it is the child of a horse.
And Rav Pappa said:

phrases.aramaic: רַבְרְבָן אוּדְנֵיהּ וְזוּטְרָא גְּנוּבְתֵיהּ – בַּר חַמָּרָא,
phrases.english: if its ears are big and its tail is small, it is the child of a donkey,

phrases.aramaic: זוּטְרָן אוּדְנֵיהּ וְרַבָּה גְּנוּבְתֵיהּ – בַּר סוּסְיָא.
phrases.english: if its ears are small and its tail is big, it is the child of a horse.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the 'we don't know her species' answer from steps 14 and 16.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the mother's species cannot be known.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: אביי and רב פפא give signs that show the mother's species, so it can be found out.

steps.title: A mute mule with ears and tail cut off
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא is about a mule with no voice and with her ears and tail cut off, so the signs cannot be used.
steps.simpleTranslation: What case are we dealing with here? A mule that is mute and whose ears and tail are cut off.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by narrowing the ברייתא to an unusual case where no sign can be checked.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A mute mule has no voice to check. A mule with her ears and tail cut off has no ears or tail to measure. So her mother's species really is unknown, and the ברייתא still does not prove that רבי יהודה is in doubt.

keyTerms.meaning: What case are we dealing with here? Used to narrow a source to a special case.
Mute (a female that cannot make sounds)
With body parts cut off (here, the ears and tail)

phrases.english: Here, what are we dealing with?
With a mute mule whose parts are cut off.
phrases.notes: 'Cut off' means her ears and tail, the parts רב פפא's signs depend on.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 17.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Signs can always show the mother's species.
steps.terutzMaskana: In this case the signs are missing, so the mother's species really is unknown.
steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא also fails as a proof. It can be about a mule whose mother's species cannot be known, so it says nothing about doubt over the father.

steps.title: So what is the final answer?
steps.stepSummary: Both proofs failed, so the גמרא asks what the final conclusion is.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the conclusion about this?
steps.whatsHappening: This short line sets up the final answer. The גמרא asks how the question from step 6 is finally decided.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof that he is sure (from the משנה) and the proof that he is in doubt (from the ברייתא) were both pushed away. The question is still open, so the גמרא asks for a final answer.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the conclusion about it?

phrases.english: What is the conclusion about it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Both proofs have been rejected, so the גמרא goes back to the open question from step 6.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether רבי יהודה is sure, or only in doubt, that the father does not count.

steps.title: Everyone forbids mating the offspring with its mother's species
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע says everyone, including רבי יהודה, agrees that mating the offspring with its mother's species is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come hear: רב הונא the son of רב יהושע said, everyone agrees that mating the offspring with the mother's species is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a clear statement to answer the question asked in step 19.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Everyone' includes רבי יהודה. If he were sure only the mother counts, a mule born from a horse would be just a horse, and mating it with a horse would be allowed. Since even he forbids it, he must be worried about the father.

phrases.aramaic: תָּא שְׁמַע, דְּאָמַר רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ:
phrases.english: Come hear, for Rav Huna, son of Rav Yehoshua, said:
Everyone agrees,
phrases.notes: 'Everyone' includes רבי יהודה. That is the whole point of the proof.

phrases.english: about the offspring with the mother's species, that it is forbidden.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע, דְּאָמַר רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 19.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי יהודה is in doubt about the father.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע: everyone forbids mating the offspring with its mother's species.

steps.title: Conclusion: רבי יהודה is in doubt
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes that רבי יהודה is only in doubt about whether the father counts, and confirms it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Learn from this that he is in doubt. Yes, learn from this.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws the final conclusion from step 20 and confirms it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה forbids mating the offspring with its mother's species, which only makes sense if the father might count. So he is not sure that the father doesn't count; he is in doubt. In practice, a mule may not be mated with its mother's species.

keyTerms.meaning: Learn from this. Said a second time to confirm the conclusion.

phrases.english: Learn from this that he is in doubt,
yes, learn from this.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the conclusion from step 20's statement.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רבי יהודה is in doubt about whether the father counts. So a mule may not be mated with its mother's species.
steps.whatToRemember: Final answer to step 6: רבי יהודה is in doubt, not sure. This replaces the conclusion of step 10, which was rejected in step 11.
steps.confusionAlert: Step 10 concluded that רבי יהודה is sure. That conclusion was rejected in step 11. The final answer is the opposite: he is in doubt.
steps.whyThisMatters: This answers the practical question from step 7: a mule may not be mated with its mother's species.

steps.title: רבי אבא tells his servant to pair mules that look alike
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבא instructs his servant to bring him only wagon mules that resemble each other.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבא said to his servant: If you bring me mules hitched to a wagon, look for ones that are similar to each other, and bring those to me.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a short story about how רבי אבא made sure his wagon mules were not a forbidden mix. This story sets up the next step, where the גמרא draws a lesson from it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two mules hitched together could break the rule of כלאים if they come from different kinds. רבי אבא's test was only whether they look and sound alike. From the earlier steps we know that voice, ears and tail show only what the mother was.

keyTerms.meaning: Mules (animals born from a horse and a donkey)
A wagon or cart that animals pull
That are similar to each other

phrases.english: Rabbi Abba said to his servant:
If you bring me mules hitched to a wagon,
look for those that are similar to each other,
and bring those to me.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the conclusion about רבי יהודה's doubt, the גמרא brings a story showing how a later sage acted in practice.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When harnessing mules together, choose ones that resemble each other in their outward signs.

steps.title: So רבי אבא ignores the father's species
steps.stepSummary: From the story, the גמרא infers that רבי אבא holds we are not concerned about the father's species.
steps.simpleTranslation: It turns out that he holds: we are not concerned about the father's seed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws the lesson from רבי אבא's instructions: he only cared about the mother's species, not the father's.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The signs רבי אבא told his servant to check (voice, ears, tail) only show the mother's kind. If he were worried about the father, matching mules by these signs would not be enough. So he must hold that only the mother counts, which is not the doubt that רבי יהודה had in step 21.

keyTerms.meaning: It turns out / evidently (introduces a conclusion drawn from what was said)
We are not concerned / we do not worry about it
The father's seed: the species of the father

steps.whatToRemember: רבי אבא matched mules only by signs that show the mother, so he holds אֵין חוֹשְׁשִׁין לְזֶרַע הָאָב: only the mother's species matters.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix this up with רבי יהודה. רבי יהודה was unsure whether the father counts, but רבי אבא clearly ignores the father.

phrases.english: Evidently, he holds:
we are not concerned with the father's seed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the halachic opinion that lies behind the story in step 22.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רבי אבא holds that for mixed-breed animals we do not worry about the father's species. We follow only the mother.
